abstract: A description is given of a blackboard architecture's basic components, and the authors enumerate the basic assumptions underlying these components. Although the blackboard framework suggests natural exploitation of concurrency, so far very few attempts have been made to exploit this concurrency. A description is given of DISPROS, a distributed blackboard architecture which serves as a general framework for the implementation of concurrent problem solving systems in multicomputer environment. The computational model of the architecture provides fault tolerance. It is shown that it can withstand all types of faults except network partitioning. The authors summarize the distributed architecture's strengths and weaknesses.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dielectric corrugated for millimeter wave applications
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: An antenna structure may be conveniently fabricated using a corrugated dielectric waveguide. A dielectric corrugated antenna has been designed and phase constants computed. By computing phase and decay constants for various corrugation thickness, corrugation period, and corrugation height, the radiation pattern can be plotted. The trapped corrugated antenna can have many useful applications. It can be used in the RF front of a radar, and beam scanning is possible. The antenna can provide high gain.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A tensor approach to understand dynamic instability in a power system and design a stabilizer
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: An explanation is presented of the dynamic instability that afflicts present-day power systems. Tensor analysis is used to compute the components of torque generated in various windings and the controller of a synchronous generator. The identification of the source of the instability is utilized to design a stabilizer which ensures stable operation at all operating conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hartley transform as a similarity transform-2D case
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Consideration is given to one-dimensional and two-dimensional discrete Hartley transforms as similarity transforms. The structure of the matrix is presented which could be diagonalized by the above transform. In particular it is demonstrated that the Hartley transform can diagonalize structured matrices richer than circulant matrices.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distributed programming with repeatable operations: experience with the MODUS file system
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A report is presented on the use of repeatable operations in distributed computations such that both servers and clients can operate in an unreliable environment without underlying software. An examination is conducted to determine how to convert nonrepeatable operations into repeatable operations. Examples are given of file operations. Repeatable operations are efficient, easy to implement and suitable for simple LANs (local area networks) for microcomputers. The MODUS distributed programming environment for Modula-2 programs is used to explore the situation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A low cost optical slotted ring network for RS-232C based communications
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A recirculating, synchronous TDM (time division multiplexed) backbone loop operating at 1 Mbps that supports multiple 9600 baud point-to-point connections, and multiple low bit rate packet channels is described. Slots are deterministically allotted to groups of devices and any medium access protocol suitable for the ring topology can be used to regulate access to the transmission channel. Nodes on the backbone are interconnected through fiber optic or atmospheric optical links. The objective of the network is to satisfy the demands of a typical computing environment, namely to offer a terminal distribution system and to simultaneously support multiple low bit rate packet channels. Devices communicate with the network through RS-232C serial lines.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A logical basis for automated interpretation of S-invariants of predicate/transition nets
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A logical basis for automated interpretation of S-invariants of predicate/transition nets is presented. It is based on proving compound logical consequences of two sets of premises derived from a given predicate/transition net: a set of global premises consisting of formulae constructed from the S-invariants and axioms of an equality theory associated with the given net, and a set of local premises consisting of formulae representing the initial marking of the net. Two algorithms for constructing formulae from two different types of S-invariants and a proof procedure for proving logical consequences of these two sets of premises within an adequate calculus of modal logic are described. The unprovability of formulae expressing progress properties is discussed, and two representative examples are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: VSATs for rural telecommunications
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A discussion is presented of the role of VSATs (very small aperture terminals) in providing rural telecommunications in a country like India. A satellite based rural telegraph network (SBRTN) is being implemented in the northeastern region of India, which contains 50 terminals. This network is primarily meant for telegraph transmission within the network as well as to the rest of the country via a gateway located near a 'hub'. While designing the network and during the studies associated with its implementation, it was found that provision for a voice transmission capability between the VSAT and hub would enhance the value of the network in different situations. The proposed access scheme and the equipment configuration at the VSAT are detailed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An expert system using ART's viewpoint mechanism to localise faults in a wide-area data communications network
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: An expert system is described which is used to isolate a faulty device on a wide-area communications network. When a complaint is lodged by a user or maintenance crew that a certain device, e.g. a printer, cannot be reached from a controller (a mainframe), then either that device is out of order or the fault lies with one of the numerous devices which connect the device to the controller. The original expert system has been successfully re-implemented using the viewpoint mechanism of ART. Putting the individual tests in their own viewpoints has enabled the loopback test to be modeled explicitly.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Project management system for C-DOT
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The authors describe a project management system that offers direct access to powerful project management tools, providing accurate and timely status reports, rapid recalculation of project schedules, and powerful resource and cost tracking capabilities. The projects in a large research organization are massive in terms of the amount of work and the number of people involved. There are many complex, interrelated activities going on simultaneously. An effective method of planning, scheduling and controlling these activities is essential for successful implementation of projects without cost and time overruns. A description is given of the different types of information required by various activities at the authors' research firm C-DOT.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthesizing LISP-programs from algebraic specifications
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A program synthesis approach based on rewriting techniques is presented. A set E of equations is taken as a specification S for a program and E is transformed into a uniquely terminating set R of rewrite rules using a Knuth-Bendix completion procedure plus special inference rules. If a specific subset P contained in R completely defines the function to be synthesized and R is consistent with S, then P serves as a (functional) rewrite program. Viewing P as an intermediate code, the rewrite rules can be compiled into LISP-code.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new method for strictness analysis on non-flat domains
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The authors address the problem of strictness analysis, particularly in the case of non-flat domains, i.e., lazily evaluated lists. Their approach to this problem is novel in that it is based on an abstract domain of very general necessity patterns which allow the requirements that a function has for the components of the data structures which form its arguments, to be modeled in great detail. The necessity patterns also allow the generation of finite abstract domains in a systematic way that can be easily customized for the application. The authors refer to the analysis using necessity patterns as a necessity analysis. This is essentially a form of backwards analysis but carried out in a different framework.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ratio parameters: a new signature for exhaustive testing
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A new approach for exhaustive testing of combinational circuits is presented. Its main advantage over other testing schemes is that the fault coverage for single stuck-at faults is significantly high. It is also established that for unate functions, all single stuck at faults and multiple stuck at faults at the terminals are testable. It seems that for irredundant realizations of general boolean functions, most of the faults also are detectable. The time needed in this approach is the same as the other existing exhaustive schemes. However, some extra hardware is needed for storage and comparison of the ratio parameters compared to the other exhaustive schemes. The technique is also suitable for the built-in self test (BIST) of VLSI circuits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A method of estimating both amplitude and phase responses of an arbitrary channel
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: An approach is presented for predicting both the amplitude and phase responses of a channel. The technique can be used to predict any type of channel, and a priori knowledge about the channel is not necessary. But any available information about the type of channel can easily be incorporated within the technique, so that it leads to better prediction. The stability problem, which is the main drawback in DFE (decision feedback equalizers) is overcome by data assisted equalization, which gives reliable estimates of the channel even at low SNR (signal-to-noise ratio). Convergence time is reduced. Finally, a method for implementing the equalizer is presented and a discussion is outlined pertinent to a suitable adaptation algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A parallel architecture for FNT and modified Winograd algorithms to compute DFT
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Fermat number transforms (FNT) are a class of transforms which operate in the integer domain. This means there will be no complex number calculations. If the base of FNT is a power of 2, then the computation of the transform does not involve any multiplications at all. A discussion is also presented of computing a discrete Fourier transform (DFT) through Winograd algorithms, wherein the cyclic convolutions are computed by using the FNT. Three cases of the Winograd algorithm are considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hardware implementation of FFT-8086 based system
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A system for the hardware implementation of the FFT (fast Fourier transform) is developed in conjunction with an SDK-86. The FFT of any number of points can be computed provided the system has sufficient memory capacity. A scheme for implementing this hardware on a PC is also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation of all-digital DPSK modems and synchronizers
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A modular program that simulates the bit error rate (BER), effects of synchronizer performance on the demodulator, performance of the demodulator under impulsive noise and block error rate (BKER) of a differential phase-shift keyed (DPSK) model is described. The DPSK modulator, receive filter, DPSK demodulator and synchronizer, and error analyzer and statistics collector program modules are discussed. Simulation results for an all-digital DPSK modem and synchronizers are presented. It is shown that such a simulation simplifiers selection of appropriate schemes for realization of circuitry.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Software development and management for C-DOT DSS
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A MAX digital switch (512 ports and beyond) has been designed, developed and placed in the field within a span of four years. After overcoming the teething troubles the system is working in the field satisfactorily. The switch is designed for multiple applications and incremental growth. The software has been developed using state-of-the-art techniques and fully exploits the hardware redundancy. Coverage is given to two major facets of the large software projects for a family of digital switching systems (DSS), i.e., the software architecture and the management.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An application of the segmentation method for the probabilistic simulation of multiple energy limited hydro units
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: An application of the segmentation method for the probabilistic simulation of multiple EL (energy limited) hydro units is presented. The authors utilize the commonly used algorithm with minor modifications. The IEEE Reliability Test System (IEEE-RTS) is considered. The applicability of the algorithm for any number of EL units, even competing for the same position in the merit order loading, is considered. The impact of a different number of EL units on the reliability, production cost, and on computational requirements is investigated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ISDN based business communication network
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The author describes an integrated digital network. The network consists of the following: (1) a business switch, (2) a digital access cross connect system (DACS), (3) a network management center, (4) a network terminator box, (5) a remote power on unit, (6) an integrated services digital network (ISDN) terminal, (7) an interface card for an IBM PC, (8) a terminal adapter, and (9) a signal convertor for mobile communication and carrier communication systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Secure communication over satellite channel
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The basic features of the direct sequence and frequency hopping types of spread spectrum communication are described in brief, and the antijam features of these systems are highlighted. Developmental efforts for spread spectrum technology during the past decade are described along with more recent spread spectrum developmental efforts at the Space Applications Centre, India. A satellite based SSMA (spread spectrum multiaccess) network design for low data rate communication to provide a jamming margin in the range of 20 to 30 dB is also given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investigation on the effect of various dithers in a noisy communication channel
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The performance of a polarity coincidence correlator with various dithers in the presence of noise is investigated. The dithers considered are of (1) the uniform type, (2) the sinusoidal type, (3) the Gaussian type, (4) the exponential type, (5) the Rayleigh type, and (6) of the rectangular type. The peak dither voltage is adjusted to be a factor 'g' of the interference peak, and SNRs (signal to noise ratios) in comparison with that of a classical correlator are plotted as a function of g. It is shown that in the presence of Gaussian noise it is best to use an exponential dither at g=1.6.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Defect detection in ultrasonic images
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The detection and characterization of defects contained in aircraft parts made of carbon composites using ultrasonic image analysis based on contour and region based segmentation methods is discussed. The experimental and analytical results show that the problems encountered in ultrasonic images are varied and require the use of different approaches for proper characterization of defects. The use of the contour based approach enabled well defined boundaries of defects and structural features to be obtained from ultrasonic images having a homogeneous background. The region based segmentation method could not differentiate between defects and structural features. A combination of the contour and region based segmentation methods enabled defect detection to be made based on geometric constraints. Other methods based on mathematical morphology also showed encouraging results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Concepts in recording of services
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A discussion is presented of the concepts in 'usage-sensitive' recording of services that are crucial to the Postal Telephone and Telegraph (PTT) system for collecting revenues for the telecommunication services offered to residential and business customers. While a lot of effort is spent on improving the transport and switching of voice, data, and image across networks, less effort is spent toward finding economical and efficient ways of recording and billing the customers. Without clear recording and billing strategies, unnecessary delays can be encountered when introducing new services. Further, with the arrival of new technologies such as integrated services digital network (ISDN), broadband ISDN (B-ISDN), synchronous optical network (SONET), and intelligent networks the functions of recording and billing become even more complex. With the aforementioned advanced technologies in mind, a description is given of the complexities in recording, and possible architectures for recording are proposed. Also, the need for selecting the 'right switching system,' that can provide flexible recording capabilities without costly field-upgrades is emphasized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Real-time control of a robotic manipulator performing a repetitive task
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A simple scheme for improving the accuracy, of a robotic manipulator is presented whereby the robot will improve its performance at a task each time the task is repeated. The system uses a series of parallel integrators which is robust to changes in the robot's parameters. The scheme is called the P-integrator controller. An on-line study of the system in the six degree-of-freedom SIR-3 robotic manipulator has indicated that a great improvement in the end points' positional errors can be achieved by the use of the P-integrator controller. Both the hardware modules and the software requirements in controlling the SIR-3 robotic manipulator are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Real time test environment for TDX-10 switching system
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: To ensure the high reliability of a large scale SPC switching system such as TDX-10 which will be the national standard integrated services digital network (ISDN) switching system in South Korea, rigorous tests should be carried out during the system development life cycle. A presentation is made of the overall requirements of the test environment and the properties of the real environment function test system (REFTS). Sample applications are given to describe how the test environment is used to allow maximum efficiency and productivity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A brief perspective on parallel programming
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A large variety of multiple instruction, multiple data (MIMD) parallel machines-some with global shared memory and some without, some with few processors to some with a few thousand processors-are becoming commercially available, and more are being proposed, designed, or developed. Programming such machines for fast execution of desired applications remains a challenging problem. An examination is made of some broad approaches towards this goal, identifying relevant issues and presenting a few guidelines that should be helpful in parallel programming research and development. The Chare Kernel parallel programming system is proposed as a solution to the parallel programming problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Concurrent program development and correctness: S2S game strategies and constructive dynamic logic
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The author summarizes work done in two areas: games for concurrency and constructive dynamic logic for concurrency. Two questions are also addressed: (1) what can be concluded in a language like dynamic logic about machine behavior if one has only partial knowledge of machine states, such as the contents of a few registers and stacks; and (2) can these computations be made naturally in constructive logic by term extraction and therefore be implementable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transputer based Hopfield neural net emulation system for pattern recognition
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A transputer-base Hopfield neural net emulation system for pattern recognition is presented. The Hopfield neural net is constructed by the transputers in mesh architectures. The cross-points of the mesh represent the basic processing element of the neural net. The concurrent OCCAM language is used for software programming and data transfer control. Using this system, certain specific pattern recognition is realized. It is shown that the performance of pattern recognition with a Hopfield neural net is encouraging and acceptable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new interframe coding scheme using the effective representation of frame difference image
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A new frame prediction technique is presented which uses the effective representation of moving areas in a frame difference (FD) image. Assuming that the luminance in moving areas of the FD image is distributed like a ridge, (valley), these areas are represented by the ridge- (valley-) line and the parameters approximating its shape. The proposed method can reduce some degradations of perceptually important parts in existing methods. From the experimental results on head and shoulder images, it is found that the prediction image of the proposed method is subjectively closer to original image than that of the block matching algorithm (BMA).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A design of a large scale telemetry network for the monitoring of remote refrigerated containers
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A sensor system to facilitate the easy access of temperature signals and digital operating condition signals from refrigerated containers has been designed, fabricated and tested. The sensor system developed is capable of accurately accessing the signals. With the use of some commercially available analog signal processing modules the RMU (remote monitoring unit) is capable of being interfaced with various types of temperature-accessing sensors. The microcontroller-based RMU is able to analyze these signals including digital inputs and serially transmit the temperature and operating conditions data to the monitoring unit at a higher level when being polled.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A modern communication system for Maharashtra police
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is given of a system which makes use of VHF medium in the band 68-88 MHz. Fairly long distances are covered through the use of hill-top repeaters. All 29 districts are connected to the State Police HQ through a special type of radio network. For this purpose the 29 districts are divided into six groups of four to seven districts each. In a group, each district terminal is connected to every other terminal in the group. Each group is also connected to HQ through a long chain of repeaters. The system can address up to 256 terminals in the network. The system provides for point-to-point or multicast messages for up to eight stations simultaneously. The system is compatible with other carriers like VFT or voice lines on mediums such as co-axial or microwave network. Its ability to work partly on one medium and partly on another is a very useful feature. The communication protocol is outlined and the mechanism for collision detection is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parallel processing architecture for high performance digital signal processing
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Currently, available digital signal processors (DSPs) offer extremely high computational performance, yet no convenient mechanism is available to solve the interconnection problem. Transputers are designed as building blocks for large processor arrays. Both hardware and software support the distribution of processes across configurations of multiple processors in a scalable way. An array of processors can be reconfigured by means of commercially available crossbar switches. A module is described that integrates the computing power of the DSP with the communication facilities of the transputer in an industry standard package.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Decompositions for optimal power flows
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Two major difficulties are experienced in most of the optimization algorithms: computational inefficiencies associated with large power systems, and problems regarding handling functional inequality constraints. The Han-Powell method has been proved to be extremely fast, robust and efficient for the small optimal power flow problems but balks at full size problems. The method can be extended to large size problems provided an efficient decomposition method is developed to overcome the problem associated with large power systems. In view of this an efficient reliable, simple and more realistic decomposition method developed by Ganga Agnihati et al. (1988) is used which overcomes the problem of large size power networks and solves the large power network using Han-Powell method. This decomposition method decomposes the large size power network into a number of blocks from the weak coupling points, and the boundary buses are modeled as swing buses.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the improvement of accuracy of recognition of handwritten numerals
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The development of a technique based on unequal weights for topological features extracted from isolated numerals is described. This technique can be used for recognition of handwritten numerals. The technique is compared with existing techniques that propose binary trees for classification. A discussion on additional topological features is also included. These features were found to be useful in some classes of numerals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a fault tolerant multiprocessor system with failsafe and failsafe-redundant interfacing schemes
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The design issues and implementation of a fault-tolerant multiprocessor system are addressed. Two design alternatives, termed failsafe and failsafe-redundant, are presented. The modular software presented previously by the authors (1989) for a tri-module redundant (TMR) system is easily transportable to the proposed architecture. The results of a reliability analysis for the two design schemes are presented. The proposed arbitration schemes can be integrated in LSI for improved reliability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Perturbations of spectrum for linear power system models
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: In a power system any change in operating condition or switching of lines may result in perturbations (in the system matrix) which are quite large. Determination of new characteristic vectors and values are computationally unattractive. In view of this, new mathematical results are presented for analyzing perturbations which are not necessarily small. A quick estimate regarding the stability and dynamic behavior of multimachine systems can be readily obtained using this technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An efficient geometric curve fitting technique
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: B-spline is a technique to trace out a smooth curve using a simple function and a set of control points. However, functional computation is usually more computationally costly than simple addition or multiplication. The Bezier method is more efficient as it is based on the geometric approach. The weakness of the Bezier method is its not passing through the control points. A geometric method is developed where a smooth, open or closed curve can be generated passing through all the control points. A weighting factor is introduced for variable curvature control of the curve to be generated. The number of points generated by the proposed method is 2/sup N-1/*(K-1), where K is the number of control points given, and N is the number of iterative steps taken.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some guidelines for choosing models for distributed database systems
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A presentation is made of results obtained from a study of the effects of model complexity on design accuracy in the context of distributed database systems. This design problem is studied with respect to one metric: average number of sites accessed by a transaction. As a result the authors conclude that the degree of complexity of a model does not necessarily reflect the accuracy of the resulting design. This suggests that designers can drastically reduce the cost and time involved in computer system design through diligent choice of system models.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distributed analyzer architecture permits real-time monitoring of heterogeneous local area networks
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: LANVista, a distributed analyzer architecture for real-time monitoring of local area networks (LANs), is described. LAN installations range from tens of nodes interconnected over a single homogeneous network, to hundreds of nodes distributed on a variety of network types interconnected through repeaters, bridges and gateways. The modular, portable architecture of the analyzer facilitates troubleshooting, analysis, diagnosis and management of multi-vendor heterogeneous LANs from a single master station. Moreover, as new networking standards emerge, the system can be easily upgraded.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evolving network services applications of SS7 signaling
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The increasing emphasis on corporate networks is resulting in a distribution of communications intelligence from the traditional central office to customer premises. This calls for Signaling System No.7 (SS7) or equivalent signaling in the interexchange carriers and regional Bell operating companies (RBOC) networks as the backbone, and the use of integrated services digital network (ISDN) basic rate interface (BRI) and primary rate interface (PRI) as the access mechanisms for these networks. The authors identify existing and near term capabilities and services that are associated with ISDN and SS7 signaling that should be considered in planning telecommunication networks in developing countries.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The unification of functional and logic languages-towards constraint functional programming
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Constraint functional programming (CEP) is presented as a new declarative programming paradigm. A CFP system is an integrated declarative programming system in which functional programming can be achieved by evaluating, expressions on the computational domains. At the same time, logic programming can also be achieved by solving constraints over these domains. CFP is developed from the notion of absolute set abstraction, a language construct in functional languages acting as the 'logic programming facility'. CFP systematically unifies functional programming and logic programming from a fundamental semantic level and is expected to provide great expressive power. Problem solving in CFP is directly performed on the intended domain of discourse. This property also allows some algorithmic constraint solving techniques to be exploited and restricts the search space in the computation to make the system efficient. CHOPE (Constraint HOPE) is defined to illustrate language aspects of CFP and examples are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CASE-a lazy version of an SECD machine with a flat environment
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: CASE is an abstract machine which supports applicative programming and is a variation of Landin's classical SECD machine (P.J. Landin, 1964). Its environment is organized in a novel way which makes variable access more efficient by removing the overhead of following a static chain or of setting up a display as in more conventional stack architectures. The CASE machine also has features allowing the execution of code to reflect lazy evaluation semantics. A description is given of the architecture of the machine, its operational semantics and code generated by a typical compiler for some sample programs. Also discussed are some optimizations made to facilitate efficient code generation on real hardware and some measurements of the efficiency of the machine.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Technology trends for advanced network services planning
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A discussion is presented of the evolution of key emerging technologies through the year 2000, that will impact the telecommunications networks globally. These technologies include photonics, software, microelectronics, artificial intelligence, and speech processing. Benefits of these technologies are already being realized in the US and other developed nations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A stochastic learning algorithm for generalization problems
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A discussion is presented of the requirements of learning for generalization, which is NP-complete and cannot be addressed by traditional methods based on gradient descent. The authors present a stochastic learning algorithm based on simulated annealing in weight space and discuss stopping criteria for the algorithm, to avoid overfitting of learning examples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modeling communications aspects in office systems
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: An approach to modeling office organization and support technology in the framework of office support systems development is presented. The main contributions of the approach are models and languages to treat, in an integrated way, both the organization and its supporting technology. Specifically, the work and the personnel organization perspectives are linked to each other in the office work description. This is very important in analysis and design since it shows how the information processing technology should cross the communication support technology within the actual work execution. This cross cannot be a sum of the two (as it is now in most applications), but has to be an integration which avoids on the one hand procedures that are self-contained and on the other that people communicate in an unstructured way.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Construction and validation of a Petri net model of a layered protocol architecture
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A study is made of a three-layer store-and-forward communication protocol as an example of describing systems in layers. The example is comprised of a 'stop and wait' transport layer built on top of an 'Aloha' data link layer implemented on a satellite communication channel; each protocol layer is modeled by a different colored Petri net which is validated independently by verifying basic functionality assertions by inspection of the place and transition invariants. A notion of equivalence in a Petri net is then introduced to study the consistency of the different layers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of algorithms for the minimization of multivalued logic functions
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A comparative analysis of the performance of the G. Pomper and J. Armstrong (1981), P.W. Besslich (1986), G.W. Dueck and D.M. Miller (1986), and the T.A. Guima and M.A. Tapia (1987) algorithms for the minimization of multivalued logic functions is conducted. The simulation results of over 15000 multivalued logic functions utilizing the MAX, MIN, and fundamental gates are obtained for each algorithm and compared to their absolute minimal results. An open ended software for the implementation of the various algorithms has been developed. The algorithms have been implemented, analyzed and evaluated to determine their relative merits. The minimized functional forms are compared according to metrics which exemplify the level of reduction in various aspects, such as the number of product terms, fundamental gates and MIN-literals. Inferences are drawn on the performance of the algorithms in general and on certain functional sets.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dependable software through fault tolerance
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The author discusses various approaches for developing highly dependable software and presents an overview of software fault tolerance techniques. Diversity is the main ingredient of fault tolerance. Various forms of diversity such as design diversity, data diversity and functional diversity and their potentials in tolerating errors in a complex software are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: System aspects of windows
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Low cost, high resolution bitmap displays available on inexpensive workstations permit the use of a new look, point-and-click style of user-interface for end computer users. Many window systems have been developed to allow application programs to adopt the graphical user-interface instead of the traditional text-oriented interface. Issues concerning the design of a window system to achieve good user and application interfaces are listed, together with the tradeoffs associated with them. In addition, the problems of building a window system to adapt to different combinations of hardware and operating systems (OS) are also described. Two prominent window systems are discussed. Their advantages and disadvantages give more insights into defining what a good window system should be.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Engineering machine diagnostic knowledge
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is presented of a joint project to develop a machine diagnostic expert system, called high vacuum evaporator diagnostics (XBAK). It is used for problem diagnosis in sophisticated manufacturing equipment used in microchip fabrication. A discussion is presented of a human diagnostician's behavior observed during the knowledge acquisition sessions, and the behavioral attributes that have been built into XBAK based on these observations. Finally, an assessment is made of the success of XBAK, and the two major limitations suffered by most current expert systems are identified.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Software development environment for TDX-10 switching system
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A software development environment for TDX-10 switching system development has been created and successfully applied in order to increase productivity and enable the production of high quality software. The environment addresses system specification design, and implementation phases in compliance with CCITT recommendations. It provides two language-based paradigms, the specification description language (SDL) environment and CCITT high level language (CHILL) programming environment, which are integrated by transformation from SDL to CHILL and by means of uniformity of user interfaces. The author introduces the environment architecture and discusses characteristics and techniques to build and integrate tools of the environments, including: the graphical environment for specification and design; user interfaces; verification and validation; program generation from graphical specification; the compilation system and programming support environment for cross-development of large switching systems; a separate compilation scheme; and source-level debugging/cross-debugging of concurrent processes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Future telecommunications services and networks
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Network capabilities are presented that have been made possible by the technological advances in the areas of photonics, microelectronics, microcomputers, and software. These capabilities will enable the service providers to meet the sophisticated user needs in a timely, cost-effective, and quality manner. Further, the authors discuss the major changes in current network architectures that will be needed to support the new capabilities in the most cost-effective manner. They conclude by demonstrating the relevance of these concepts to developing countries.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An inductive approach to finding fixpoints in abstract interpretation
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A new method for finding fixpoints in abstract interpretation, based on the technique of computational induction, is presented. This technique has the advantage that it allows elements of the fixpoint to be computed separately without restricting the size of abstract domains which can be handled. Since abstract interpretation typically only requires one or two elements of the fixpoint in order to test some property of a program, it is expected that in the general case this method will perform better than any of the other methods. The well known technique of strictness analysis is used to introduce abstract interpretation. Other techniques for finding fixpoints are briefly reviewed. It is first shown how to apply the method based on computational induction to strictness analysis, then the more general case is considered. Dealing with nested function applications and mutual recursion is demonstrated. Analyses involving higher-order functions are discussed briefly, and the overall correctness of the approach is examined. An example of an analysis featuring non-flat domains is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A comparison of various VSAT multiple access techniques with reference to the Indian context
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Factors relevant to very-small aperture terminal (VSAT) networks in India, including service requirements by the user, RF spectrum utilization, space segment position, and indigenous manufacturing capability are discussed. A comparison of code-division multiaccess (CDMA), time-division multiaccess (TDMA), and frequency-division multiaccess (FDMA) techniques for satellite communications using VSATs is presented. The comparison is based on services required, space-segment utilization, and extent of frequency coordination.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design of a uniform interface between adjacent layers (protocols)
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A functional analysis and design schemata are presented for a generic communicating entity with the aims of characterizing its elementary components, suggesting their organization, providing a general model to design protocols, and exploiting the functional decomposition to locate the elements which can be treated as being layer independent and used as modular components of the design. In line with that, the interface between adjacent layers is considered as an abstract data type to provide information hiding, a uniform module independent of the layer and to allow easy tuning and dimensioning of the system by means of simulation. The proposed functional analysis and design schema are addressed to properly locate well known layer elements and provide a general framework to design and develop communication protocols.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A Petri net simulation model of HDLC
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is given of the development of a model for the simulation of the high-level data link control (HDLC) protocol, which is the standard data-link layer protocol in the open systems interconnection architecture. The architecture is constructed using the PROTOB simulation environment, which allows an object-oriented system description based on a class of colored timed transition Petri nets called Prot nets. The main features of the HDLC protocol are briefly summarized and a quick overview of the features of PROTOB is provided. How PROTOB can be used to model communication protocols is discussed. An outline is presented of the choices that led to the actual implementation of the HDLC protocol model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parallel execution of equational programs
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Equational programming is a style of declarative programming with very simple semantics, based on logical consequences, which coincides with the traditional semantics of mathematical expressions. Sequential evaluation strategies for such programs are well known. However, not much seems to be known about evaluating equational programs on parallel computers. An overview is presented of a research project initiated for developing compilation and execution techniques for parallel evaluation of equational programs. Topics discussed include the following: the case for lazy evaluation; path sequential systems and parallel evaluation; parallelism in equational programs; automatic extraction of parallelism; and load balancing and load estimation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computing in commercial banks: analyses of social and organisational impacts
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The reasons for computerization in banking are discussed, emphasizing the computerization of banking activities in India. The manner in which information technology enables banks to contain working and administrative overheads, widen the scope of services and improve the quality of decisions and the work environment is examined. It is indicated why failure to adopt this technology in banking may affect the marginal competitive position being held by the developing countries in service sectors. The problems arising out of implementation of the technology regarding their social, political and financial implications are categorized. A critical review is made regarding the impact of computing on employment from different perspectives. The possible impact of computing on management and organization is evaluated. A review is presented of the rationalistic approach which is used to explain the impact of computing and the political motives behind systems development.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: TENCON '89. Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference. 'Information Technologies for the 90's' E/sup 2/C/sup 2/; Energy, Electronics, Computers, Communications (Cat. No.A89CH2766-4)
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON

articleTitle: Hypergraph based topological design of large multibus systems
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The topological design of multibus systems is considered. The problem consists of finding a system with as many processing elements (PEs) as possible under constraints on the number of PE ports, the number of PEs connected to the same bus and the system diameter. Earlier works on this subject used either combinational structures (e.g., balanced incomplete block designs, or BIBDs), or graph theory. The authors use a very natural approach to this problem, namely hypergraph theory. They present two methods to construct hypergraphs with diameter one and two. Finally, the authors develop a technique, called hypermultiplication, to build up larger hypergraphs from smaller ones, with a small increase of the diameter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of exchange dimensioning system using artificial intelligence approach
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is given of the features and design principles of exchange dimensioning system, DIMEX-10, which offers interactive support for assisting telephone company personnel in the installation and production of the TDX-10 digital switching system. The dimensioning process determines the volume of an exchange component in both hardware and functional terms. DIMEX-10 uses artificial intelligence techniques and employs novel representations to denote the knowledge required for exchange dimensioning.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Network performance analysis of packet-switching C/sup 3/ system
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A packet-switching computer network used in the C/sup 3/ system is introduced. This network analyzes packet delays in channels with various data rates, and optimum channel capacity is given in various packet input rates. The result obtained from a simulated testing system is the same as that of the theoretical analysis. It proves that the analysis is universally applicable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A parallel sorting algorithm for C-DOT parallel processing system
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A parallel processing system is being developed. Unlike conventional parallel architectures, the parallelism is at the level of an algorithm. A sorting algorithm for this machine is presented. The architecture of the parallel messing system consists of an elevated single instruction multiple data (SIMD) model that works at the level of a basic algorithm. Viewed from another angle, the architecture of the multiple instruction multiple data (MIMD) type, since synchronization is not at the instruction level. In reality, it is midway between SIMD and MIMD, which the author calls an SAMD (same algorithm multiple data) architecture. The philosophy is to divide the problem into a number of algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An ADPCM with an exponential power estimator based predictor for speech coding
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The application of the exponential power estimation (EPE) technique to realize computationally simple predictor adaptation algorithms has been investigated. An adaptive differential pulse code modulation (ADPCM) system which employs the EPE-based adaptive predictor provides a computational advantage of 2N multiplications (N being the predictor order) and one division per iteration compared to the ADPCM which employs a block power estimator based adaptive predictor. A performance comparison has been conducted with two conventional ADPCM systems at different bit rates and channel conditions, using different quantizer characteristics. The results indicate that the proposed ADPCM performs identically to the conventional ones at 32 kbps and better than them at 16 kbps.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An intelligent decision support system for stock investment
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is given of an effort that attempts to combine artificial intelligence, computer networking and database and management science technologies to aid stock investors in their decision making processes. Data from a multi-database environment, including the investors' own databases as well as those public databases coming through modern communication networks are retrieved using natural English language. Portfolio analysis and other forecasting techniques are then applied to the data. Thus, a stock investment analyst is able to obtain extremely wide sources of information and assistance with minimal computer knowledge. The system, called Stock Investment Aid, has been implemented using the Hong Kong stock market as an example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Efficiency optimal operating for vane-speed parallel flow control system
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: In a flow control system with a fan, the variable speed drive is becoming popular because of its cost-effectiveness compared with conventional vane or damper flow control systems. But, for the large system which requires the parallel operation of several fans, it cannot always be said that driving all the fans with variable speed is the best or most cost-effective choice. In this regard, a variable speed drive fan and a constant speed drive fan with vane control under conditions of parallel operation are dealt with. The total energy consumed in the vane-speed parallel flow control system depends on the operating points of the fan speed and the vane opening, and three will exist an optimal combination of the speed of one and the vane opening of the other that minimizes the total power consumption. This optimal combination is derived from a mathematical model and tested on actual fans for a generating boiler system. The results confirm the validity of the theoretical analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: M-hop interception of FH/LPI signals using autocorrelation techniques
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A decision algorithm in the correlation domain taking advantage of the large time-bandwidth is surveyed to see the effect of weighting, epoch error and in-between frequency distance for the single-hop case, and of extension to the M-hop case. After extending the integration interval to M hops, the asynchronism effect is shown to be compensated. The performance of a hard decision for M-hop using per-cell decision and BMWD (binary moving window detector) is shown to have better performance than the soft decision.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Signal resolution using generalized eigenvalues for coherent sources
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: New results are presented for resolving two or three uncorrelated/coherent plane wave sources in the presence of white noise, when subspace-based high resolution estimators are used to estimate the directions of arrival of incoming signals. The signal to noise ratio required to resolve two or three closely spaced sources is derived in various source scenes. The results are compared with those corresponding to a two uncorrelated/coherent source scene.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SNAIL: a simulation tool for connectionist networks
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: SNAIL is a general purpose connectionist network simulator. The simulation system introduces a language for the purpose of defining connectionist networks and running simulations. Trial simulations performed using SNAIL indicate that the resulting simulation tool is simple, flexible and modular. The system is general purpose in that a wide variety of connectionist networks-varying in every detail from network topology to the learning algorithm-can be dealt with easily. SNAIL has been implemented in LispTalk, an object oriented programming system running on top of Lisp.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Extended Pascal for SIMD processing
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: An extension of Pascal for single instruction multiple data (SIMD) processing is proposed. The language is architecture independent and model independent. An attempt is made to provide the programmer with greater power for exploiting the interconnection network pattern using several routing and masking schemes. The desirable features of Pascal are carried over in this extension of Pascal. The authors have analyzed the power of the new constructs and the facilities through numerous case studies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance analysis of (M,L) algorithms
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The performance of the (M,L) algorithm applied to the decoding of convolutional codes is investigated. Asymptotic analytical results and simulated points for low values of the signal-to-noise ratio are presented. Different versions of the algorithm are compared; in particular, the influence of the decoded path continuity on the performance is explored. The results obtained by simulation at low signal-to-noise ratios show that optimal detection can be achieved with a saving in the number of retained states by a factor of two. Asymptotically, a memory saving of one order of magnitude is foreseen from the analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of voice synthesis algorithm using redundant bit reduction technique for the text editing type recorded announcements
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The speech synthesis techniques applicable to the recorded announcements of an ESS (electronic speech synthesis) system are discussed with regard to high-quality text-editing-type synthesis at a medium data rate (10-20 kbps). The hybrid coding techniques are useful for solving certain problems, but are not desirable for the word-based synthesis due to pitch change. The authors propose a hybrid coding scheme that can control the pitch and the data rate according to the quality. This technique is applied to a synthesis algorithm for the recorded announcements of the ESS switching system in Korea.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automated computation of cardiac ventricle volume from two-dimensional MRI data
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A computer based system is described that has been developed to automatically determine ejection fraction from an automated analysis of two-dimensional, serial slice magnetic resonance image, (MR1) data. Using a General Electric 1.5-T MRI system, twenty images, per-cardiac cycle along with sixteen simultaneous 5-mm anatomical slices were obtained from each patient. Automated algorithms, using frequency histogram based computations, were used to preprocess the raw image data and to enhance the contrast between the blood pool and the myocardium. Contour data, defining the blood pool in the left ventricle, were automatically generated from adjacent, sequential image slices and used to estimate left ventricular volume as a function of time. Results from normal volunteers indicate that this system could provide a useful clinical diagnostic tool for visualizing and quantifying regional left ventricular function.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The introduction of hidden units to optimizing neural networks
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A systematic approach to deriving neural network algorithms that promotes the introduction of hidden units and defines their best features is presented. To illustrate the method, the authors derive a neural network for the NP-hard integer knapsack-packing optimization problem. Preliminary simulation results have been promising, especially in light of the ease with which viable network parameters have been found. In the course of subsequent research, the authors have found the method to be applicable to bin-packing, multiprocessor scheduling, and job-sequencing problems as well.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A non-preemptive monitor for real-time applications
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Requirements are described for real-time tool sets and details are given concerning NAMO, a non-preemptive application monitor for real-time applications. The design goals and system features are outlined. The authors give preliminary details of this system since some of the subsystems are still in the process of development. An example of applying NAMO to a real-time system which is resource limited is provided.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive noise subtraction to improve the performance of range tracker at low SNRs
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: An analysis is made of the split gate discriminator (SGD) used in radar range tracking and it is shown that when the signal to noise ratio (SNR) is poor, an SGD operating at the output of a square-law envelope detector can give a large error. The authors propose an adaptive noise subtraction technique to improve the performance of SGD for low SNRs. Simulation results are presented in support of the theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The CPqD Telebras CHILL programming environment
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is given of the CHILL (CCITT High Level Language) programming environment developed as a platform for a telecommunications system. The programming environment provides an integrated set of software tools that enable software engineers to produce the reliable and efficient real-time software required by modern digital telecommunication systems. A general overview is presented of the software tools that currently constitute the programming environment, how these software tools relate to each other, how they can be used in the development, maintenance and fast evolution of complex concurrent CHILL programs and how the programming environment exploits current LAN (local area network) and workstation technologies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dataflow analysis of Prolog programs
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Dataflow analysis, used by optimizing compilers, can be applied in the static analysis of Prolog programs. A general flow analysis algorithm is presented which can be used to derive predicatewise information about the input program. This algorithm has been specifically applied to solve the mode inference problem, but can also be used for other applications such as parallel execution, intelligent backtracking and garbage collection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A microprocessor based position controller for a laser optical grating
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A microprocessor controlled system for precise positioning of laser optical grating is discussed. A stepper motor controlled by a dedicated microprocessor system tunes the position of optical grating used in the optical study of Nd-Yag pumped dye lasers. The monitor program makes the system user friendly and the user can operate the system very easily. The hardware and the software of the system are explained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The flow control of an integrated voice/data LAN
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: It is shown that the optimal flow control in an integrated voice/data local area network (LAN) combines control data average arrival rate with the time assignment speech interpolation (TASI) technique. The control principle is a window type mechanism (bang-bang control). In the analysis of the TASI technique, a two-dimensional Markov chain with the state transition diagram in general material is converted to a birth-death link. Numerical results are given which are of great value to integrated services digital network (ISDN) flow control design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A mechanism for interconnecting high-speed hosts and LANs via an ATM network, and analysis of its end-to-end delays
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A mechanism is presented for interconnecting high-speed hosts and high-speed local area networks (LANs) via an asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) network. Also presented are upper bound estimates of the end-to-end delays for varying conditions of network traffic. The mechanism uses a simple bandwidth arbitration scheme among network end-points to avoid focusing while interconnecting high-speed end-devices operating at rates ranging up to 100 Mbps. From the delay analysis, it is found that the mechanism presented is viable, especially when the end devices are expected to exchange large data blocks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Validation of C-DOT DSS family of switching systems
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Carrying out validation plans successfully is one of the key factors in developing a family of switching systems for a developing country. A discussion is presented of the various requirements that a good validation plan should meet. The work draws heavily on the authors' experiences in this area. The authors provide practical considerations and tips on how to make a good validation plan and conduct the validation exercise more fruitfully. Wherever possible, the authors articulate some interesting conflicts that typically arise in forming and carrying out validation plans. Tools and techniques that are required for validation are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new method for estimating Markov random fields
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A method is introduced for estimating the parameters of Markov random fields from complete or incomplete data. The method is computationally more efficient than its best competitor, the method of maximum pseudo-likelihood. For incomplete data, the method leads to an algorithm which is similar to, but simpler than, the EM algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Overlay network applications for network modernization and positioning for the future
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A digital overlay approach is described that a PTT/telecommunications administration can effectively utilize to meet its telecommunications modernization needs. This approach allows the PTT to create a digital backbone network in an overlay fashion, and interconnect selected nodes of the public switched telecom network (PSTN) to the overlay network. Through this approach, the PTT can selectively modernize the network, improve the quality of service, and introduce new services based on subscriber needs. In particular, the overlay strategy allows the PTT to move its high calling rate subscriber traffic from the PSTN to the overlay network, thus improving the call completions for this traffic. The needs of each subscriber group are examined, and the problems encountered while modernizing are discussed. It is shown how an overlay network can resolve some of the problems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: R&D at Telebras-CPqD: the TROPICO RA project
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A summary is presented of Telebras R&D activities, highlighting the TROPICO system, which is an integrated family of digital switching equipment. The first two elements of the TROPICO family (TROPICO C AND TROPICO R) have already been completely industrialized and installed in the Brazilian network. The first commercial exchanges for TROPICO RA were installed in 1990. Efforts to attain a high degree of technological independence in telecommunications has proven to be very successful.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A PC based voice mailing system
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The design and development of an IBM PC/AT-based low-cost voice mailing system (VMS) is described. This system, targeted for small to medium organizations, can receive and store incoming telephonic messages. The called party can later use an ordinary touch tone telephone to access his own private area on the system and do operations like playing back or deleting messages. The VMS consists of cards that can be plugged into the PC/AT bus slots and master software running on the PC/AT under the OS/2 operating system. In its maximum configuration, the system can simultaneously handle four subscriber lines from an EPABX and is estimated to support around 150 users.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Colour vision for industrial applications
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A vision system for colour object recognition is presented. The proposed system is low in cost and sufficiently fast and reliable for simple industrial applications. The system comprises a fiber optic illumination system lenses, a camera, a frame grabber and an IBM PC/AT microcomputer with a colour monitor. DT 2853/2873 frame grabbers are used for digitizing the image. The recognition algorithms are based on red-green-blue and hue-saturation-intensity modes. The approach and development of these algorithms are elaborated. The accuracy, reliability and speed of recognition has been very good. The recognition is based on closest path, thresholding and mathematical modeling algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A cost effective production philosophy for C-DOT
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Summary form only given. CDOT's (Centre for Development of Telematics) digital switching system is designed to meet wide ranging technology, a variety of applications and different manufacturing capacities, with a range of approaches to investment and manufacturing. The system architecture provides high reliability, modularity, fault tolerance, flexibility and expandability. The system meets CCITT standards, and can withstand stringent environmental conditions. The manufacturing of CDOT's products is based on a simple assembly line principle. Simplicity has been the focal point in the production philosophy.
