The manufacturing philosophy can be adopted to different investment proposals, different lines of products and their product mix. A factory automation system based on an IBM PC network has been developed for integrating purchasing, material management, production, shop floor control, marketing and sales, financial management, etc.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: C-DOT DSS-maintenance software
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Switching systems are expected to meet stringent performance criteria, in order to meet the high availability requirements laid down for them. To meet these requirements, major emphasis is placed on reliability, quality of service and maintainability, in the Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT) digital switching system (DSS). A robust hardware/software distributed architecture is developed. Within this architecture a loosely coupled recovery strategy is adopted, in which an error is confined and recovered in the module where the error is detected. C-DOT DSS has a wide range of automated capabilities, which provide it with the capability to run with no need for manual intervention. These maintenance functions are capable of handling multiple failures and severe malfunctions. However, a wide variety of user friendly maintenance functions are provided which give the maintenance personnel overriding powers. The flexibility, fault resilience, and user friendly maintenance capabilities are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated services digital network voice data manager
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A discussion is presented of the integrated services digital network (ISDN) voice-data manager (IVDM) application being researched by the PC division of the National Cash Register (NCR) Corporation, Dayton, Ohio. This application is geared toward taking full advantage of the basic and supplementary voice services and basic data services (file transfer, screen transfer, etc.). The various implementation level issues of IVDM which runs under the multitasking environment offered by OS/2, are examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Estimation of shallow slot effect on the permeance of doubly-salient structures (stepping and switched reluctance motors)
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Two sample calculations for finite slot depth performed using the assumed flux paths method have been carried out and it has been found that the estimated correction factors are overestimated for d/s above 0.5 and underestimated for d/s below 0.4 (in comparison with the finite element computation). The maximum and minimum difference between the two calculated values are 3.6% and 1%, respectively. Considering the approximate nature of the assumed flux paths method the combined procedure used for this calculation shows good agreement with finite element computation and the result can be used at least for handy reference.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Compile time vs. runtime: scheduling parallelism on dataflow machines
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Summary form only given. Exploitation of parallelism in programs decreases execution time but increases resource requirements. It is argued that this problem should be addressed by applying compile-time analysis and static scheduling techniques. Such techniques have been developed for scheduling loops on very long instruction word (VLIW) machines which, like dataflow machines, can exploit fine-grain parallelism in programs. In VLIW machines, all resources can be scheduled very precisely because of the synchronous model of parallelism. It is shown how these techniques can be applied to dataflow machines by adopting a less rigid notion of scheduling providing a reasonable trade-off between parallelism and resource usage. The authors also show how such asynchronous scheduling can be implemented in a novel dataflow loop schema for the Monsoon Explicit Token Store dataflow machine.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CDOT PBX: an evolution
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is given of the evolution of a PBX. The background in which the first product was launched, the market situation at that time the need for such a product are discussed. The system, features, enhancements in terms of capacity and user features are described. The transfer of this technology to the licencees, the process and its effect on the market are also presented. Finally the ongoing and envisaged applications of the system along with the need and plans for future development of this product family are outlined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An automatic focusing visual inspection system for die inspection
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Automatic focusing of a visual inspection system is described. A vidicon camera was mounted on top of a high powered microscope to capture an image, process it and send an appropriate signal to a stepper motor which controls the movements of the microscope. The method used is based on the acutance of the video signal waveform. Acutance is a measure of the steepness of the video signal waveform. It implies that a sharp image will have a sharp gradient of the gray level across the image. This is measured vertically and horizontally and used to control the movements of a stepper motor to achieve an optimal focusing state. On achieving it a signal from the control circuitry of the automatic focusing system will be sent to the control circuitry of the die inspection machine to determine whether the die is good or a reject.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of a DSP FM demodulator in the presence of noise
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The signal to noise ratio (SNR) characteristics of the demodulated signal is analyzed and confirmed by simulation. Taking into account an application to an FM broadcasting receiver, an analysis and simulation are carried out with various parameters such as input carrier to noise ratio, number of quantization digits and construction of a 90 degrees phase shifter in a DSP (digital signal processing) demodulator. Demodulation processing is implemented by a 32-bit CPU. Simulation results show that a sufficient SNR can be obtained using an A-D converter, which is introduced in the IF stage, having only 6 and 9 quantization digits for monophonic and stereophonic signals, respectively, without appreciable increase of input signal power over what is required when an analog demodulator is used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Real time power system simulation for training purposes
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The use of simulator training for operators of generation/transmission/distribution grids has increased dramatically. The development of operator training simulators, however, depended on the availability of economical computational hardware. In addition, models and algorithms to simulate large power systems in real time required significant innovation. Although better models and algorithms continue to be developed, the emphasis on research today is not on still higher fidelity but on features that enhance training. A review is presented of the state of the art of operator training simulators for terrestrial power systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interworking between access protocol and network protocol for interswitch ISDN services
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The authors depict the interworking required between E&M and integrated services digital network (ISDN) protocol and between E&M and Signaling System 7 (SS7). Possible scenarios are given for interworking between ISDN access and SS7 protocols to extend ISDN supplementary services interswitch, in particular, those services that require ISDN user part (ISDN UP). The examples chosen to depict interworking are call forwarding, user-to-user signaling, and call waiting.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Personal computer based internal unity power factor control of ASCI fed synchronous motor drive
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A new control strategy, internal unity power factor (IUPF), for operating an ASCI fed self controlled synchronous motor drive (SCSMD) is proposed. Analytical expressions to determine steady state characteristics of the ASCI fed SCSMD based on the proposed control strategy are obtained. It is shown that the IUPF operation and optimum airgap flux control of ASCI fed SCSMD enable the drive to operate at maximum torque and higher efficiency at all loads and speeds. The use of a personal computer for implementing the proposed control strategy in real time is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Singular value computations on a massively parallel machine
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Consideration is given to the computation of the singular value decomposition (SVD) on the Connection Machine (CM). Brief descriptions are given of the *Lisp language and some typical matrix manipulating functions. Implementation details of various Jacobi-SVD algorithms on an 8192-processor CM are presented. For n*n matrices, where n<or=64, the methods compute the decomposition in time O(n) per sweep. It is shown that the Connection Machine offers a highly efficient programming environment for SVD computations. Common bottlenecks, such as processor synchronization and data partitioning, are absent. The SIMD (single instruction multiple data) architecture is simple to use, and only minimal attention needs to be paid to the actual hardware configuration. The one-to-one matrix element to processor map means that, on a 65536-processor model, there are enough physical processors for n*n SVD problems so long as n<or=256.<<ETX>>

articleTitle: Effect of phase noise on the performance of coherent optical fiber communication system
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The purpose of this work is to calculate the PSD (power spectral density) of 5B6B coded signals at the output of a PSK (phase shift keyed)/FM subcarrier heterodyne system. The influence of laser phase noise on the PSD has also been investigated. Experimental results indicate that as the laser linewidth decreases, a sharp peak is obtained at the frequency, f, equal to the sum of the IF and source oscillator frequency and the bandwidth of the signal at the output decreases. The value of PSD at f, for the linewidths of 10 MHz, 15 MHz and 20 MHz are 1.21*10/sup -18/ W/Hz 0.81*10/sup -18/ W/Hz and 0.607*10/sup -18/ W/Hz, respectively. This shows that the average power is greater when the laser linewidth decreases. The result obtained may be useful in the design of multichannel coherent communication systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Tomographic approach to acoustic noise mapping in shallow sea
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A method for the acoustic noise mapping of a shallow ocean using a tomographic approach is presented. The output of a planar array of hydrophones in the ocean is expressed as a weighted line integral of the acoustic field. A set of measurements of the array output for different steering directions and several array locations can be inverted using an algebraic reconstruction technique to reconstruct the acoustic field. The tomographic approach yields fairly good results even though no deconvolution of the array output was done and a small number of arrays was used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Telecommunications-policy issues
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Policy, equipment manufacture, service delivery and regulation are the four constituents of telecommunication services, and how and by whom these should be addressed/delivered is being inquired into by country after country, leading to the de-governmentalization, corporatization and introduction of competition in several countries. A discussion is presented of the four elements of telecommunications services, matching new services to new markets and, rewriting existing telecommunication laws.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Preparation of theoretical ionograms for Delhi and analysis of Delhi ionograms (C/sub 4/-recorder) with it, to study production rates (q/sub 0/), loss rates ( beta /sub 0/) and scale heights (H/sub 0/) in F/sub 1/-F/sub 2/ transition region
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The basic points in the preparation of theoretical h'F curves (overlays) for the low latitude station at Delhi and the necessity of renaming them theoretical ionograms are summarized. Significant results regarding q/sub 0/, beta /sub 0/, H/sub 0/, T/sub 0/, and T/sub infinity / obtained as a result of analyzing the Delhi ionograms (C/sub 4/-recorder) around F/sub 1/-maximum are discussed. The theoretical ionograms are discussed and compared with results obtained using other techniques. It is concluded that these theoretical ionograms can be equated with the actual ionograms of ionospheric recorders and can be prepared for any station whose propagation constants are known or for any location where the installation of a ionospheric recorder is difficult.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parametric blends for shape modeling
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Blends are surfaces that arise in manufacturing and do not usually appear on blue-prints. Methods are presented for modelling them in CAD/CAM systems. Modelling of two types of blends for parametric surfaces is considered; rolling sphere blends and general cross-section blends. The blend surface design task is split into two subtasks: identification of the normal cross section as well as the path followed by it. The path is identified as the intersection of the offsets of the given two surfaces. The offsetting technique establishes a natural parametric correspondence between the two blend boundary curves. The design of the shape of the cross section curve is left to the user. This provides the flexibility demanded by the application at hand.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: International telecommunication systems and networks
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: VSN's (Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd.) international telecommunication services are described. The following services are offered: (1) telephone, (2) telex, (3) telegraph, (4) private leased services, (5) television, (6) press communications, and (7) packet data. These services are operated over the following transmission systems: geostationary (synchronous) satellites operated by Intelsat; wideband submarine telephone cables; line of sight microwave; co-axial and digital optical fibers; and HF radio. In addition to these transmission systems, international gateway switching systems are used for switching of telephone/telex lines and messages and data. These include the following: (i) analog stored program controlled (SPC) telephone switches; (ii) SPC telex switches; (iii) SPC message switches; (iv) gateway packet switches; and (v) digital telephone switches.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experimental performance evaluation of the clustered multiprocessor system MUGEN
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The MUGEN multiprocessor system comprises 32 microprocessors which are clustered into 4 groups, each containing 8 processors. The authors report on a system software and the parallel languages (para-C) developed on MUGEN, which assist application programmers. By using these tools, the authors have evaluated the performance of MUGEN, which uses the Livermore loops. A comparison of the efficiencies for single instruction multiple data (SIMD)- and multiple instruction multiple data (MIMD)-type processing on MUGEN is also reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel technique of data compression for spoken word recognition systems
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A technique is described for data compression which helps in reducing the storage of data per reference/test word without degrading the recognition accuracy. An effort has been made to solve this problem in two stages. Feature extraction of the voice sample is performed using a conventional filter bank speech spectrum analyzer to get a time domain representation of the speech signal into time averaged frequency domain descriptions known as frames. The second stage of data compression deals with the reduction of the encoded crude data matrix. The number of rows in the data matrix of a word is reduced to a uniform size of rows. This data compression technique is based on the variable time segment coding of individual frequency channels. The performance of this technique was evaluated for the recognition of spoken isolated words using a Z-80A microcomputer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: TDX-10: software structure and implementation
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is given of the structure and the implementation of the TDX-10 software, which is a large-scale electronic switching system with distributed control architecture. The system structure is layered into three levels, a system, a subsystem, and a block. A system, the top level, is divided into many subsystems, each devoted to a specific function. Each subsystem is broken down into many building blocks which consist of several program files. As a basic loading unit in a processor, an execution module is generated by compiling files for a block or for a few blocks. A function could be simply inserted/deleted into/from an existing system by just adding/deleting its relating blocks in the system. Most peripheral processor (PP)-level programs, written in assembly or C-language, are combined with hardware units in the block for the easy maintenance of a system/block with a concept of a virtual machine.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A story understander using rhetorical structures
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Story, a form of coherent text, is hard to analyze and understand for the computer because of the intricate interaction among the sentences and its strong cognitive nature. A novel method is presented for understanding stories using psychological and narratological reflections on memory models and prose analysis. Based on the methodology an implemented story understanding program is also described. The program has been tested using a number of fables.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fault tolerance-a software approach
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is given of the design and implementation of FToS, a fault tolerant system implemented with a software approach. FToS is a low cost fault tolerant system, well suited to online applications. It is application independent and guides the application in data updates and application startup and shutdown. It follows the approach of redundancy, but unlike conventional redundancy, FToS allows additional hardware to be utilized to its full capacity when there is no failure. The current implementation is on Unix System V.3.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of impulse noise on digital UHF radios in suburban areas
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is given of low capacity digital UHF radios of varying capacities from 6 to 120 channels developed for transmissions to rural areas. Due to fast urbanization and haphazard growth, impulse noise due to manmade sources is increasing in Indian urban and suburban areas. Two- and eight-Mb/s UHF radios are field tested in the presence of impulse noise. After field feedback, they are found superior to their analog alternatives for voice, VFT and voiceband data. The error performance is analyzed and countermeasures are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simple estimators for HF channel estimation
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A comparison is made of four different estimators, for estimating the sampled impulse-response (SIR) of an HF radio link that is designed for the transmission of analog speech signals. The particular application studied is the transmission of digital data at 4800 bit/s, employing a serial quadrature phase shift keyed (QPSK) signal with a carrier frequency of 1800 Hz. The HF radio link is modeled as having three different Rayleigh-fading paths (sky waves). System 1 is the conventional gradient (least mean square, or LMS) estimator while system 2 is the gradient estimator with degree-1 least-squares fading memory prediction. Systems 3 and 4 are novel and are developments of system 2. Results of computer simulation tests on the four different estimators are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dynamic models for software reliability assessment
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A class of models for describing the behavior of software failures is presented. The models fit into the framework of dynamic general linear models. The motivation for the models and inferences made using linear Bayesian methods are discussed. Finally, the models are applied to some actual software failure data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Generation of binary sequences for cryptographic applications
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Probability theory of binary random sequences is used to characterize Boolean memoryless combining functions of n variables producing an output binary sequence Z. This is used to define conditions on the truth table of the function such that the latter is a m/sup th/ order correlation-immune. Algorithms to generate m/sup th/ and (m+1)/sup st/ order correlation-immune functions of (n+1) variables from a m/sup th/ order correlation-immune function of n variables are also derived.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design an intelligent programmable logic controller with IPLC
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is given of the intelligent programmable logic controller (IPLC) software package, which was designed in the inferencing language Prolog. IPLC provides front-end intelligence for the programmable logic controller. IPLC has the ability to analyze, intelligently, plant system knowledge held on a computer so as to make decisions on how to control a process. IPLC is able to generate ladder logic programs for the PLC and synthesize a new control routine when a fault is reported on the process plant.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A browsing method for image database on the microfilm library devices
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A microfilm retrieval system was developed. The system has the following features: browsing, interfacing of the ISDN (integrated services digital network), networking between the microfilm and a computer and easy operation using a mouse. The contents of many books and materials have been copied into the microfilm retrieval system already. The retrieval system can be used for long distance access. It has a multimedia database structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer aided design of millimeter-wave transmission systems
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A more generalized dielectric waveguide has been analyzed using the effective dielectric constant method. The dispersion characteristics have been plotted for such new structures as the diagonal dielectric guide and E-H plane dielectric guide. Experimental data show that the cutoff frequency is higher in the E-H plane dielectric guide as compared to the diagonal dielectric waveguide for identical dimensional parameter and dielectric material.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CHILL toolset for C-DOT DSS
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The CCITT high-level programming language (CHILL) is a tool that helps to improve the quality of computer controlled telecommunication systems. The efforts of the Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT) to set up a CHILL environment to support its telecommunication software development are reported. The CHILL toolset being developed is described in detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: IOCR: an intelligent optical character reader
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Intelligent optical character reader (IOCR) for reading printed English text with alphanumeric symbols is presented. There are seven major functional units in the system: a self trainer, a graphic editor, a database manager, a token extractor, a pattern matcher, a spelling checker and a guess by feature analyzer. The first three units provides facilities for reference pattern manipulation, while the last four units are for character recognition. The spelling check and the feature analysis are based on some intelligent statistical rules, and together they enhance the recognition rate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A logic programming based specification animation tool for real-time systems
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: During the elicitation and verification of the specification for real-time control systems, the sequential-temporal aspects need to be treated separately. These aspects also require animation for verification and incremental refinement of the specification. An automated tool kit can be used to mechanize animation of specification. An augmented Petri net modeling tool is adopted to capture the logical, sequential and timing dependencies of a real-time control system. A description is also given of a logic-programming-based animator for automated animation of the Petri net description. The augmentations involve a predicate net approach and temporal extensions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: TELEINFO-an application of text-to-speech technology for remote database query
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: TELEINFO (telephonic access to information) is a subsystem that connects an incoming telephone line to the application system on the Unisys A-Series mainframes. Database access is not direct but through an existing application software such as the Manufacturing Resource Planning (MRPII) System, Global Financial System, etc. The authors demonstrate how text-to-speech technology coupled with current telephone operation can be used to increase productivity, make information retrieval easy and improve the customer services. A description is also given of the application of TELEINFO software to manufacturing resource planning.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bipolar ECL implementation of SPARC
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The scalable processor architecture (SPARC) defines a general purpose 32 bit RISC processor architecture. The simple nature of the architecture provides a migration path to higher performance levels as new technologies become available. The goal was to design an architecture that would scale with, or track, improvements in the circuit technology. It has been implemented in gate arrays, full custom CMOS and bipolar emitter coupled logic (ECL) technologies by four different vendors. A number of implementations in other technologies including BiCMOS and GaAs are underway. A description is given of the B5000, the bipolar ECL implementation of the SPARC architecture. Also covered are some of the system level considerations that influenced the design of the processor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: NWD hosted UHF based rural telecom: a new horizon in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Beginning with the structure of the telecommunication system, a discussion is presented of the actual and projected telecommunication facilities available in rural Bangladesh. The discussion covers the telegraph service, the rural public call office, the upazila telecommunication system and, nationwide dialing (NWD). The rural telecommunication projects are presented with starting and completion dates.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Corporate telecommunication networks using CDOT 128P PBX
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is presented of the potential applications of CDOT 128P/256P PBX in the emerging area of private networks called corporate networks. The authors show how a digital PBX, viewed to date as an intraoffice communication device, can be used for wide area interpremises networking. An outline is also presented of the major benefits of using private networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An object-oriented architecture for cooperatively integrated information systems
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: An experimental method of designing cooperatively integrated information systems from an architectural point of view is proposed. The approach is a top-down method, based on a framework of relational databases and the object-oriented paradigm. Additionally, this approach has greater flexibility and adaptability than the traditional approaches.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Verification of hardware descriptions at the functional level
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A method is presented for the functional verification of designs at the register transfer level. The verification of correctness is taken as a basic specification of the design given in a functional specification language. The verification procedure is based on the identification of observable control signals (OC) and observable actions (OA) in the specification and design descriptions. The OCs and OAs are then taken as a base for the conversion of the descriptions to graph forms. The graphs, reduced by graph grammars, are then used to extract two sets of regular expressions: one representing the sequence of control signals and the other one the sequence of actions taken in response to the first ones. Finally, the verification procedure checks if the sets of the specification are subsets of the design's sets.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: KMDS-an expert system for integrated hardware/software design of microprocessor-based digital systems
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: An integrated design automation system, KMDS, is presented for the design of microprocessor-based digital systems. It is implemented using a knowledge-based expert system to support the following functions: (1) automatic synthesis of the circuit of microprocessor-based digital systems at the processor-memory-switch level, (2) automatic generation of control programs for the implemented microprocessor-based digital systems, (3) automatic ASIC design to realize special-purpose circuit functions at the algorithmic level, (4) automatic printed circuit board layout, and (5) high-level knowledge base editing and debugging. In addition, several features are included to help realize a modularized and flexible design automation tool.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An intelligent vision system for inspection of packaged ICs
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A visual inspection system for recognizing defects in IC packages is presented. In this system, the iconic domain of two-dimensional gray level image analysis based on the feature extraction method is used. A software package is developed to carry out the extraction of defects that may exist on the IC leads and the surface of the IC chip. The recognition of these defects is achieved by comparing the image data with a predefined threshold value. To improve the speed of performance of the system, an auto-windowing routine is incorporated in the system to map out the relevant areas for image processing. The inspection algorithms and various processes used by the system are outlined. From the experimental results obtained, it is shown that high accuracy and good reliability can be achieved by the proposed system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transmit-receive array design for high resolution source location
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: An approach is presented to super-resolution imaging of point sources using active arrays of transmit/receive elements. The usual techniques of high resolution imaging using passive receive arrays often fail for coherent point sources. Data obtained from transmit/receive arrays may be arranged to form observation matrices to which eigenspace direction of arrival estimation may be successfully applied, even in the presence of coherent sources. This approach provides great flexibility, which derives from the variety of arrangements available for the observation matrix, and it provides insight into the design of the array.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Data network evolution and software development environment
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The evolution of data communication networks as a reaction to telecommunication regulatory relief in the USA is discussed. The NYNEX INFO-LOOK information gateway is used to illustrate trends in the evolution of the data network architecture. How this affects software development technology is also discussed. Software development environments for communication systems required a system architecture which allows for fast and efficient software development. Architectures for data communication networks will be changing dramatically in the near future. This will require development environments with flexibility so they can adapt to changing network architectures and information processing hardware. Such an environment is referred to as the rapid development environment (RDE), to express its capability for fast adaptation to new network architectures and implementation hardware.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some further properties of homogeneous immittance polynomials
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Some of the theorems of homogeneous immittance polynomials are discussed. The ratio of consecutive terms of such polynomials will be a homogeneous multivariable positive real function. Another theorem that is considered deals with the decomposition of homogeneous immittance polynomials. Necessary and sufficient conditions for such a decomposition are derived.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A software environment for general purpose MIMD multiprocessors
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A software environment for general purpose multiple instruction multiple data (MIMD) machines based on packet switched message passing paradigms is described. The environment provides system calls for communication between various processing elements in the machine and system calls to get the configuration of the system. It assumes the presence of a host processor through which facilities are provided for forking remote processes on various processing elements. The host processor has all the peripherals of the system and acts as an I/O processor of the system. During the normal course of execution, it forks processes, collects results from various processing elements, sequences them and then produces the output of the program.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An expert system for diagnosis of electronic equipment using structural model and trouble-shooting heuristics
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is given of a personal computer implementation of an expert system for the diagnosis of electronic equipment. The expert system employs mixed mode reasoning. It reasons from first principles using a device specific hierarchical structural model and is guided by a universal trouble-shooting control strategy, and heuristics. The structure of an analog or digital electronic device is viewed as a hierarchical interconnection of modules and is represented as a semantic network. A reduced behavioral description records the normal expected behavior. It is not used for simulation, thus saving computer power. A structure analyzer sub-system processes the semantic network to infer topological relationships and performs signal propagation. During execution the expert system cycles through the three major steps of trouble-shooting: candidate selection, checkpoint recommendation, and inference.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimal acquisition of PN codes
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: An adaptive technique for acquisition of pseudonoise (PN) sequences with the variable thresholds required for PN detecting chips is proposed. The Robbins-Monroe stochastic approximation procedure is applied to evaluate the adaptive thresholds under the constraint of fixed signal power. It is demonstrated that the proposed scheme achieves the theoretical lower bound derived on PN acquisition time.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a fast packet switch for ISDN
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The fast packet switching technique is proposed in order to integrate switching networks related to different classes of information. A suitable architecture for the implementation of the fast packet switch is selected on the basis of various comparison criteria, and the design and implementation of the switch fabric is discussed in detail. The interfacing of this switch to the existing network is also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PC communication in an OSI environment-TM&T: Mail and Talk on TAINS
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: TAINS (Tohoku University Academic Information Network System) is an open systems interconnection (OSI)-based large-scale information network. A very large number of the users of TAINS are using personal computers (PCs). Few of them, however, have any sort of network interface, therefore PCs are connected to TAINS via a communication adaptor called the CS (communication server), which enables PCs to communicate via the in-house coaxial cables and the optical fiber trunk line in accordance with the ISO 8802.3 protocol. The development of a communication application, TM (TAINS M&T Talk system), which is designed to provide PC users with electronic mail (E-mail) and simultaneous keyboard talking (E-talk), is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reflections in computer vision
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is given of how reflections can be analyzed for the determination of 3-D surface orientations. The analysis is carried out for a simple situation involving a single visible polygon and its reflection. The problem has a single degree of freedom and is underconstrained. Hence, some a priori information is needed to determine the exact surface gradients.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digit recognition using energy envelope and zerocrossing rate
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A speaker independent isolated digit recognition algorithm is described. Decision making using a tree structure has been adopted in this method. Two simple features, energy envelope and zerocrossing rate, have been used for the classification. An 80% recognition accuracy with trained speakers has been achieved with this algorithm. This method implemented on a 386 super PC/AT could respond within 20 sec.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Direct design of spatio-temporal preprocessors for direction estimation of wideband sources
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The authors formulate the direct design of focusing filters, a one-step filter coefficient computation procedure which avoids explicit evaluation of the frequency response. Various aspects of the proposed design technique are discussed. Simulation results are presented to substantiate its effectiveness.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic evaluation of pronunciation in language classes
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: An experimental system is proposed for language courses to teach correct pronunciation to foreigners. A dynamic programming technique is applied to compare the student's voice with model pronunciation. Several important features are automatically extracted and as a result the student's pronunciation is evaluated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CHILL for parallel processing
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The author discusses the growth potential in the field of parallel processing. The general requirements for a parallel language are listed, and a description is presented of the features provided by CHILL (CCITT high level language) for concurrency. Enhancements which will widen its suitability for various general requirements of a parallel language and which cover a variety of applications are suggested.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Notice of Violation of IEEE Publication Principles: On computing code word utilization for component coded digital video
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract:
Notice of Violation of IEEE Publication Principles

"On Computing Code Word Utilization for Component Coded Digital Video"
by P.J. Kulkarni, P.P. Kulkarni, N.R. Phadnis
Proceedings of the Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference (TENCON), November 1989, pp. 678-681

After careful and considered review of the content and authorship of this paper by a duly constituted expert committee, this paper has been found to be in violation of IEEE's Publication Principles.

This paper copied figures and text from the paper cited below. The original content was copied without attribution (including appropriate references to the original author(s) and/or paper title) and without permission.

"Code Utilization for Component-coded Digital Video"
by D. Izraelevitz and J.L. Koslov
Proceedings of the 16th Annual SMPTE Television Conference, February 1982, pp. 22-30


In the component coded digital video, luminance, (Y) and two color difference components (C1, C2) are separately converted to digital. The components are computed by multiplying red-green-blue (RGB) vectors by a matrix. This component matrix has a special structure in the sense that the color difference components become zero for white or gray shades being encoded. The matrixing operation alters the dynamic range of the computed, Y, C1, C2 components compared to the dynamic range of RGB signals. A mathematical treatment is presented by which the effect of quantization of these components on dematrixed RGB signals is studied; the efficiency with which a color system utilizes component codes can thereby be calculated. It is shown that of all the word combinations available for quantization, optimum code word utilization is only 25%. Matrices are presented for the optimum code utilization.<>

articleTitle: TDX-10 recorded announcement system using ADPCM coding technique
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The interwork, hardware configuration, and design specification of a recorded announcement system are presented. The system, which is called the ready-made message announcement system (RMAS), has been developed for the TDX-10 electronic switching system. The main function of the system is to give the calling party an announcement message of why a call was not completed and what further action should be taken or to announce a message as a special service when a call was processed normally. RMAS consists of a software unit, an announcement primary-function software unit (APSU), and a hardware unit, called the announcement primary-function hardware unit (APHU), which is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive coherent-signal subspace algorithm for direction estimation and tracking
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A new adaptive algorithm is proposed for adjusting the coherent noise subspace of the coherently averaged covariance matrix (CACM) by a constrained least-squares search. The proposed estimator possesses a superior rate of convergence and good tracking properties. All simulations confirm this prediction. The algorithm incurs greater computational cost at each iteration and has a tendency to become numerically unstable. Fortunately, the use of double-precision arithmetic can eliminate the instability problem. also the systolic array implementation developed in recent years may achieve real-time processing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Decomposing functional programs for parallel computation
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: An approach is presented for automatically decomposing functional programs for execution on a multiprocessor system. A program is translated into combinator code and it is compiled into fixed program code for evaluation by one or more stack machines. The decomposition of the resulting target code is handled dynamically at runtime. This capability is introduced through the use of a set of combinators whose defining properties play a direct role in the allocation, synchronization and deallocation of processors. The authors have developed a fixed program multiprocessor simulator and are conducting performance evaluation studies to determine the effectiveness of this approach to parallel computation. Results from these studies are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A multi-channel formant speech synthesis system
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The design and implementation of multi-channel formant speech synthesis system is described. The aim of the research was to develop a system capable of producing up to eight channels of high quality synthetic speech, concurrently. The signal processing bandwidth necessary to achieve this goal required the design and implementation of a custom application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) which performed the signal processing functions associated with a formant speech synthesis algorithm. A description is also presented of the synthesis system and the ASIC architecture developed to implement the formant synthesis functions and to achieve the design goals. A fully synchronous bit-serial signal processing architecture is described which is used to implement the synthesis functions, and it is shown how the increased signal processing bandwidth available from this approach can be utilized to achieves multi-channel synthesis operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: TBC-host processor interface for IEEE 802.4 token bus applications
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The development of the interface between the token bus controller and a single board computer is described. The authors present, in detail, a functional description of the hardware circuits in the interface. The design and structure of the software developed with a basic operating system are also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sequentially adaptive neural networks
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A sequential adaptation scheme for neural networks is proposed. The scheme is formulated as equality constrained optimization tasks. The approach taken in developing the scheme is based on the geometric point of view of pattern recognition and on methods of surface interpolation. The set of training equations for the radial basis function network of Gaussian nodes is developed, and an experiment on its classification performance is carried out.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: FDDI technology in a public backbone network
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is given of a project whose objective is to specify and construct a pilot metropolitan area network based on fiber distributed data interface (FDDI). The testing phase began in May 1989 and the full pilot network consisting of four class-A stations was operational in July. FDDI has been chosen because there is an immediate need for connecting local area networks (LANs) together and distributed queue dual bus (DQDB) is not available yet. The pilot network is a 34 km long dual network using single mode fiber and single mode to multimode (SM/MM) converters. Currently the network consists of four Ethernet to FDDI bridges. The goal is to develop testing and measurement methodology for FDDI based networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design, development and study on a S-band pulse compression radar
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is given of studies carried out on a linear FM pulse compression S-band radar. The details on the subsystems used are given. The maximum detection range and resolution have been predicted and experimentally confirmed. Typical oscillograms on echo patterns are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: TROPICO-RA O&M and quality assurance
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: A description is given of the main quality assurance procedures carried out for TROPICO RA during the project and the O&M (operations and maintenance) facilities. TROPICO RA is a switching system designed to fulfil all international quality of service recommendations. For this purpose, TROPICO RA's project life cycle has many procedures for quality assurance to design hardware and software items within a specified quality level. The quality of service can be divided into reliability and grade-of-service requirements. TROPICO R structure (first element of the TROPICO family of switching systems) is highly reliable as it was designed for graceful degradation and load sharing. TROPICO RA uses the same design philosophy and incorporates new solutions in order to improve the reliability performance. The grade-of-service requirements of TROPICO RA have been extensively evaluated for its specified traffic capacity. To validate these requirements during operation, the system is always measuring and recording traffic and performance data. It is able to give instantaneously any information needed for traffic flow control and routing decisions. These important O&M functions are performed without using call-processing resources.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A distributed problem solver for seismic monitoring
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The authors propose a distributed problem solver, implemented on a suitable layered architecture supported by a computer network, as an automated tool for seismic studies. Four expertise levels have been identified. Each one corresponds to a suitable knowledge domain inside of which experts work to find a synergic solution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Program synthesis in equivalent specifications
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: An exploration is made of the possibility of synthesizing a definition for a derived operation based on a given specification of an abstract data type. The starting point is a sufficiently complete definition of this operation given in a different, but proven equivalent specification of the same abstract data type. It is shown how the completion procedure allows one to synthesize such definitions and the authors give sufficient conditions to ensure the sufficient completeness of the synthesized definition.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: International switched digital service
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: International switched digital service, an evolution of domestic switched digital services that should complement existing private line digital services between the USA and other countries is discussed. With the increasing inter-dependency between international communities, there was a perceived need for dial-up and usage-priced digital transport services that are ubiquitous. AT&T, as a service provider, is responding to such a need with the phased introduction of international switched digital service between the USA and other countries. Public switched digital services in general, and international switched digital service in particular, are recognized as a test bed for future international high-speed switched digital services, such as NxDSO specifically 384 kbit/s, and 1536 kbit/s, and thus stimulate and create new opportunities in the USA and other countries. A summary is presented of the feasibility of extending switched digital services to the international community.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: TROPICO-RA digital exchange hardware structure
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: TROPICO-RA is a stored program controlled switching exchange which is now at its final development stage. A description is given of its hardware structure. It is shown how the solutions were shaped by the high reliability and adaptability requirements for the many configurations, applications, and evolution which characterize the TROPICO equipment family.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An artificial intelligence approach to trouble-shooting in automatic test equipment
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: The need for ATE (automatic testing equipment) and its advantages over manual testing and diagnosis are discussed. The importance of an expert system using rule-based techniques to test and trouble-shoot radio equipment is considered. The test system software kernel solves the problems using a computer model of expert human engineering, implementing AI (artificial intelligence) techniques. Automatic diagnostic aids locate faults specifically and rapidly using a fault dictionary (rule knowledge file), a guided probe or a combination of both.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A Boltzmann machine solution of the traveling salesperson problem: a study for parallel implementation
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Neural net algorithms are intrinsically parallel. They are also often used for solving difficult optimization problems. It is therefore natural to investigate the speedup which might be obtained by implementing a neural net algorithm on a parallel architecture. This work explores that question by looking at three possible implementations of the traveling salesperson problem (TSP) on a binary Boltzmann machine. These three implementations vary in their degree of parallelization. The results suggest that there are important relationships between the amount of speedup obtainable and the quality of solutions obtained. A general framework for studying such questions is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Broadband applications characterization
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Broadband networking refers to data transmission at rates above 2 Mb/s and up to 600 Mb/s from the customer interface. Today's local area networks are evolving towards fiber distributed data interface (FDDI) at 100 Mb/s and metropolitan area networks based on IEEE 802.6. The integrated services digital network (ISDN) is expected to evolve towards broadband ISDN by the middle of 1990. The applications of these high speed networks though generally known are not well understood. The author has identified, described, and classified some potential broadband applications. A general framework for characterizing these applications is described. The focus is on the data applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance analysis of software: CDOT case study
publicationTitle: Fourth IEEE Region 10 International Conference TENCON
abstract: Software quality assurance involves checking and assuring if aspects such as the design, coding, testing and performance of the software are as per the specifications. There have been many attempts to quantify the quality of the software and many quality metrics have evolved. Quality attributes are measured in various ways. Two of the ways in which performance can be gauged are (i) by measuring the time required for execution of the functions and (ii) by the number of problems found during testing. These two aspects are discussed taking the Centre for Development of Telematics (CDOT) as an example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
